doc.title: Earl Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002

title: Oakland's Swing Club: Eckstine, Hines, Wardell Gray and Vernon Alley's group
summary: He saw Eckstine's band with Blakey and Miles at the Swing Club, then Wardell Gray's path to Goodman's bebop band.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: John Kirby’s small band, they brought in Jack McVea and they brought in Eckstine’s big band with Art Blakey and all those cats and I got to see that. They brought in Fatha Hines and I’d go down there on a regular basis, never dreaming that someday that our paths would cross musically. But who was in that band: Wardell Gray was in the band, Kermit Scott, who you’ll see on some of the early Billie Holiday records, Kermit Scott the tenor player. And they both left the band while it was here and so they got who else? That was the Fatha Hines band. But with the Eckstine band, I don’t know how it happened but one day, I lived up there, and one of the times I went back and Miles was in the band. So I don’t know whose place he took because I didn’t know the personnel but I was just watching the band and watching Art Blakey. Because at that time you know, we had to watch him to see what he was doing. He was a powerhouse. And so anyhow then Hines’ band came in and then Wardell left and Wardell — Vernon Alley put a little group together with Wardell in it and Gerald Wiggins. Yeah. Wiggins had gotten out of the service. Gerald Wiggins and Wyatt Ruther, Bull Ruther, the bass player. He was with everybody, Basie, Lena, Buddy Rich. It’s easier to say who he wasn’t with. Anyhow this was around 1947 so Vernon had put this group together. And so he had Wiggins and Wardell, himself, and who was on piano? He had — oh Wiggins. Wiggins was on piano. He had this quartet. And so they worked around here for a while then Wardell went to Los Angeles and he ended up with Benny Goodman, with Benny Goodman’s bebop band.
Yeah, the one that had Doug Mettome and the piano player who later turned into a vocalist. I can’t think of his name.
He had Charlie Kennedy on alto.
That group didn’t last too long, did it?
It’s funny you know if you think of Benny Goodman trying to go with the musical style. I mean he ended up—
